title: Black Americans have an increased rate of angiotensin converting enzyme inhibitor-associated angioedema
authors: Brown NJ, Ray WA, Snowden M, Griffin MR
followUp: 51,752 person-years of ACE inhibitor use, 1986 to 1992
population: Tennessee Medicaid participants aged 15 years or older prescribed ACE inhibitors
funder: not read: the publisher page is not accessible and the PubMed abstract carries no funding statement. PubMed lists grant FD-U-000073 from the US Food and Drug Administration.
result: 82 confirmed cases of angio-oedema, 1.6 per 1000 person-years of ACE inhibitor use. Adjusted relative risk in Black against white users 4.5 (95% CI 2.9 to 6.8); first 30 days of use against more than 1 year 4.6 (2.5 to 8.5); lisinopril 2.2 (1.2 to 3.9) and enalapril 2.2 (1.4 to 3.5) against captopril; hospitalisation within the previous 30 days 2.0 (1.1 to 3.6). Dose and concurrent diuretic use were not associated with risk.
